PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
JOINT APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICE CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES
Direct Testimony of Intervenor Virginia Zizelmann, Trustee of the Trusts Tammy Z Ahlgren 2004 Investment Trust and the Christine R Vickrey 2004 Investment Trust
 in Opposition to Segment F8 and Offering Alternative Routing


My name is Virginia Zizelmann and I am trustee for the Tammy Z Ahlgren 2004 Investment Trust and the Christine R Vickrey 2004 Investment Trust which includes Tract 5207 which is bisected by segment F8. The adjacent properties together are 314 acres and are treated as one holding. 
The property consists of a 61 acre river bottom on the North San Gabriel leased for hay production and grazing and a ridgeline rising to the elevated section to the balance of the property which is also leased for grazing. I have been notified that the line may affect the ability to lease the property for grazing in the future. Cattle grazing may be affected but the abundant wildlife will definitely be hurt both by the initial construction and loss of habitat. Hunting is not allowed, and deer and turkey populations are significant. 
USDA entomologists with The Smithsonian Institution visited the property on a survey and collection of insect specimens in Texas and New Mexico. They only found their target Curculionidae insect on Tract 5207. It lives in a very unique habitat. They also commented on the total diversity and volume of insects and asked to return in the future for additional collecting.
 The entire bottom flooded in the July 2025 floods. The area where the proposed powerline would cross the river had flood waters higher than the four to five foot fences. Large trees were toppled and floated with force down river. There was a large volume of debris that blocked access for weeks. Any towers would need to be able to withstand significant impact and any repairs could be delayed due to high water and debris.
Entrance to the property will have to pass under the proposed power line and there are no roads accessible by large equipment.  The river bottom cannot be traversed in rainy weather either for construction or major repairs. There is a light gravel road that would bisect the line that serves as the main entrance. The gate limits vehicles to approximately   10’ in height and weight is limited by a welded pipe cattle guard.
John Zizelmann purchased the property 27 years ago not as an investment but to provide a rural setting for family and friends to enjoy nature and the wonderful views provided by the 100’ elevation. His ashes and those of his father were both spread on the property, and there is no intention of selling this property for generations.  The proposed line would negate the intended use.
Alternative Routing
Exhibit A
As marked, there is an existing powerline and easement as close as 5,000’ to F8 in more than one place. Tract 5207 would be about 4,000’ from the existing line and the proposed line would be about 10,000’. It appears that the total length of either route, F8 or existing right of way, would be about the same. 
There should be no structural difference since F8 does use the existing powerline easement when it approaches Texas 195 as marked by two parallel lines. Further, 16 Texas Administrative Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B) requires that transmission facilities be routed, to the extent reasonable, to moderate impacts on affected landowners and communities including the use of existing compatible rights-of-way where appropriate.
Virginia Zizelmann
2223 Bolsover St
Houston, Tx 77005
